headline: Google's Watch Beat Your Doctor's Blood Pressure Check — In One Study
author: unZappedTV
text:
Google's Watch Beat Your Doctor's Blood Pressure Check — In One Study

Google's watch beat your doctor's blood pressure check — in one 196-person study. Google Research put AI on a regular smartwatch's pulse (PPG) and motion sensors, with no cuff calibration, and tested it against the gold standard: a 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitor. Published in Nature, Nov 5, 2026.

What the study found:
• The watch caught 65.8% of people with high blood pressure; a single initial office check caught 55.3%. Both had 90% specificity
• So the watch still missed about a third of people
• In a smaller follow-up group (n=48, people with a high office reading), multi-day home cuff monitoring caught more (89.2%) than the watch (78.4%)
• Google calls it early feasibility research; the findings helped inform the Blood pressure trends feature

The feature: Blood pressure trends in the Google Health app, on Pixel Watch 3, 4 and 5 (included) and Fitbit Edge / Fitbit Air (Google Health Premium). It gives no numbers — just a monthly High / Not high. If it says High, Google recommends 7 days of readings with an upper-arm cuff, then share them with your doctor. "Not high" doesn't promise your blood pressure is normal.

To be clear: Google says this is a general wellness feature — not a diagnosis, not a hypertension prescreener, and not a replacement for a blood pressure cuff or your doctor. Not for use during pregnancy. This video is not medical advice.
